name: TLE2141 / TLE2142 / TLE2144 (TI Excalibur low-noise high-speed bipolar)
tagline: TI Excalibur complementary-bipolar amp: 10.5 nV/rtHz, 5.9 MHz, runs on up to ±22 V and drives 10 nF loads. A niche pick found in some high-end DAC output stages.
technology: Complementary bipolar (TI Excalibur process), internally compensated; single (TLE2141), dual (TLE2142), quad (TLE2144); A-suffix = tighter-precision grade

lineage.notes: Part of TI's Excalibur complementary-bipolar line. Standalone per-device datasheets (e.g., 'TLE2142, TLE2142A, TLE2142Y') came first. A combined TLE214x/TLE214xA datasheet, SLOS183, followed in February 1997.

PCN20250730004.1 (31 Jul 2025) adds RFAB (Richardson) as a fab site using TIB process technology, alongside DL-LIN (Dallas). The die revision moves from B to C and the datasheet from SLOS183D to SLOS183E. First ship 29 Oct 2025.

key_specs.condition: performance relatively independent of supply over this range

reputation.summary: A niche, lightly discussed part among hi-fi hobbyists. In Head-Fi op-amp rolling threads, one poster says a 4300-euro Acoustic Arts DAC uses eight TLE2142s in its output stage. One user liked its tonality, body and bass. Another was not impressed compared with the LM4562. There is no broad consensus.
typical_uses: DAC output stages (per a Head-Fi report on an Acoustic Arts DAC)
op-amp rolling in headphone amps / DACs
caveats: Praise is sparse and mixed: one Head-Fi user preferred the LM4562.
Parts made from late October 2025 may be die revision C (RFAB, TIB process). No listening or measurement comparisons with older die B stock have been found.
The Acoustic Arts DAC claim is second-hand from a forum post and has not been independently verified.

revision_history.changes: First combined TLE214x/TLE214xA family datasheet, replacing the per-device datasheets.
Last old-format revision. Detailed changes not seen. Dates of revisions A–C unknown.
Moved to TI's new datasheet format. Issued under PCN20250730004 (RFAB fab option, die revision B to C, BOM options). The specific spec-table changes were not seen.

A search summary confirms the header 'SLOS183D - FEBRUARY 1997 - REVISED OCTOBER 2012' (radiolocman copy). Its front-page specs: 15 nV/rtHz at 10 Hz and 10.5 nV/rtHz at 1 kHz, 10,000-pF load capability, 20 mA minimum short-circuit output current, 27 V/us minimum slew rate, 5.9 MHz GBW, and 500 uV maximum Vio at 25 C. The change list against revision C was not shown.

revision_history.doc_number: unknown (standalone 'TLE2142, TLE2142A, TLE2142Y' per-device datasheet, pre-SLOS183)
revision_history.changes: The old per-device edition (title 'TLE2142, TLE2142A, TLE2142Y EXCALIBUR LOW-NOISE HIGH-SPEED...', icbase copy) includes the TLE2142Y chip-form device. Its description, as seen in a search snippet, mentions a 'patent-pending' input stage giving 10.5 nV/rtHz with a 6-Hz 1/f corner and a symmetrical 40 V/us slew rate into loads up to 800 pF. Another snippet, probably from the current TI text, says a 10-Hz 1/f corner. Which snippet came from which copy is not certain, so this possible spec or wording change needs checking against the PDFs.

silicon_changes.when: PCN20250730004.1 issued 31 Jul 2025; proposed first ship 29 Oct 2025
part_numbers_affected: TLE2142 (likely; same SLOS183 datasheet, not explicitly confirmed)
silicon_changes.identification: Die revision C (was B) and RFAB fab-site codes on reel/box labels. Date codes after late October 2025. Datasheet SLOS183E instead of SLOS183D. Existing DL-LIN (Dallas) die-B material may ship in parallel.
silicon_changes.summary: TI qualified RFAB (Richardson) using TIB process technology as an extra fab alongside DL-LIN (Dallas), with a die revision from B to C, a datasheet update from SLOS183D to SLOS183E, and new assembly BOM options. This is part of TI's multiyear move off 200 mm factories. TI states there is no anticipated impact on form, fit, function, quality or reliability.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown. A new die on a different process under the same part number could change noise, distortion or stability details. No measurements or listening comparisons found.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: new die and process under an unchanged part number. TI claims no form/fit/function change, but the SLOS183E spec tables have not been compared with rev D.

counterfeit_notes: No specific counterfeit reports found in this pass. As with other TI DIP op-amps sold on marketplaces, buy from authorized distributors. Note that genuine post-October-2025 stock may be die revision C from RFAB.
alternatives: LM4562 / LME49720 (named in a Head-Fi comparison)

claims_confirmed: The family datasheet is SLOS183 'TLE214x, TLE214xA Excalibur Low-Noise High-Speed Precision Operational Amplifiers'; rev D is Feb 1997, revised Oct 2012 (https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/data.html?%2FTLE2142=&di=330795)
Current revision SLOS183E is dated July 2025 and is in the new format (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/slos183e/slos183e.pdf)

PCN20250730004.1 (31 Jul 2025, first ship 29 Oct 2025) adds RFAB with TIB process, changes die rev B to C, and moves TLE2141's datasheet from SLOS183D to SLOS183E; no anticipated form/fit/function impact (https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/7170/PCN20250730004.1.pdf)

Specs: 10.5 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz, 15 nV/√Hz at 10 Hz, 5.9 MHz GBW, 27 V/µs min slew, 340–400 ns settling, 150 ns saturation recovery, 20 mA min short-circuit current, 10,000 pF load capability (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tle2142.pdf)
Performance is relatively independent of supply over ±2 V to ±22 V (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tle2142.pdf)
An older standalone 'TLE2142, TLE2142A, TLE2142Y' datasheet exists on a third-party mirror (https://www.icbase.com/File/PDF/TTI/TTI20590106.pdf)
TLE2142-Q1 has its own TI datasheet and product page (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tle2142-q1.pdf)
TI product pages exist for TLE2142AM, TLE2142AM-D and TLE2142M-D (https://www.ti.com/product/TLE2142AM-D)

revision_chain_notes:
TI is the only vendor found. No second sources or acquirer re-issues turned up for TLE2141/2142/2144.

Revision chain, oldest to newest:
(1) Pre-1997 per-device datasheets. The dual sheet is 'TLE2142, TLE2142A, TLE2142Y EXCALIBUR LOW-NOISE HIGH-SPEED PRECISION OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIER' (icbase TTI20590106.pdf, already listed). Singular-title copies that probably belong to this generation are datasheet4u/datasheetspdf 1442138 (TLE2142) and 1442136 (TLE2141), and semiconductors.es. Their literature number(s) and dates are still MISSING, as are any separate TLE2141 and TLE2144 standalone lit numbers.
(2) SLOS183 original, February 1997: the combined TLE214x/TLE214xA sheet. No copy has been identified as holding it.
(3) SLOS183A, B and C: dates and copies still MISSING. None of the 4 searches surfaced these letters. Likely holders are older aggregator scrapes (digchip, datasheetarchive, alldatasheet 28934 TLE214X / 228137 / 201893), but none showed a header.
(4) SLOS183D, 'FEBRUARY 1997 - REVISED OCTOBER 2012': confirmed again from the header in the search summary (radiolocman di=330795).
(5) SLOS183E, July 2025: new-format sheet on ti.com, tied to PCN20250730004 (RFAB fab, die B to C).

A possible text change between the old per-device edition and later SLOS183 text was seen: 'patent-pending' input stage with a 6-Hz 1/f corner versus 10-Hz. It needs checking. The derivative datasheets (TLE2141-EP, TLE2142-EP, TLE2144-EP, TLE2142-Q1) have unknown lit numbers and revision chains.

The archive seed URLs follow TI's standard legacy URL patterns (focus.ti.com symlink, and a slos183d revision-specific path modelled on the confirmed slos183e path). They were NOT seen in search results and should be treated as candidate Wayback lookups only.
